partners.diseaseBName: neurodevelopmental disorder with microcephaly, short stature, and speech delay
partners.mechanism_chain: TRAPPC10 (HGNC:21795) —DISRUPTS→ ER-Golgi trafficking (GO:0006888); ER-Golgi trafficking (GO:0006888) —LEADS_TO→ Abnormal skin development (HP:0000951); ER-Golgi trafficking (GO:0006888) —LEADS_TO→ Microcephaly (HP:0000252); ER-Golgi trafficking (GO:0006888) —LEADS_TO→ Short stature (HP:0004325); ER-Golgi trafficking (GO:0006888) —LEADS_TO→ Speech delay (HP:0000750); COL7A1 (HGNC:2568) —DISRUPTS→ ER-Golgi trafficking (GO:0006888); COL7A1 (HGNC:2568) —LEADS_TO→ Nail deformity (HP:0000954). Loss-of-function mutations in TRAPPC10 disrupt ER-Golgi trafficking, leading to neurodevelopmental abnormalities including microcephaly, short stature, and speech delay. While COL7A1 is primarily known for its role in collagen production and skin integrity, severe phenotypes of epidermolysis bullosa can also involve defects in intracellular trafficking pathways. Therefore, disruptions in ER-Golgi trafficking (GO:0006888) due to mutations in TRAPPC10 and potentially COL7A1 (in some severe EB forms) can lead to overlapping cellular dysfunction manifesting as diverse phenotypes including skin abnormalities and developmental defects.

partners.mechanism_chain: COL7A1 (HGNC:2207) —DISRUPTS→ Collagen VI assembly and secretion (GO:0007173); Collagen VI assembly and secretion (GO:0007173) —LEADS_TO→ Golgi apparatus-mediated protein trafficking (GO:0048784); NSF (HGNC:7870) —DISRUPTS→ Golgi apparatus-mediated protein trafficking (GO:0048784); Golgi apparatus-mediated protein trafficking (GO:0048784) —LEADS_TO→ Congenital localized absence of skin (HP:0011224); Golgi apparatus-mediated protein trafficking (GO:0048784) —LEADS_TO→ Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy (HP:0011347). **Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-204005)

**Proposed mechanism:** COL7A1 (HGNC:2288) —DISRUPTS→ Extracellular matrix organization and remodeling; LMAN2L (HGNC:25686) —DISRUPTS→ Extracellular matrix organization and remodeling; Extracellular matrix organization and remodeling —LEADS_TO→ Congenital localized absence of skin (HP:0000972); Extracellular matrix organization and remodeling —LEADS_TO→ Intellectual disability (HP:0001249). Mutations in both COL7A1 and LMAN2L disrupt the shared pathway of extracellular matrix organization and remodeling. This disruption leads to the distinct phenotypes of skin defects in epidermolysis bullosa and intellectual disability in IDDM69.

**How to falsify it:** The absence of mutations in COL7A1 or LMAN2L in individuals with either disease, or the identification of mutations in entirely distinct pathways for each disease, would falsify this hypothesis. _(variant: The presence of common variants (AF > 0.01) in gnomAD within the coding regions of COL7A1 or LMAN2L that do not segregate with either disease would weaken the hypothesis.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of COL7A1 and LMAN2L in extracellular matrix organization could reveal novel therapeutic targets for both skin integrity and neurological development, potentially through modulating extracellular matrix components or signaling pathways.
